title: Open finite Cartier zero-divisor locus for a line-module morphism
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:Y\to T$ be proper, flat and finitely presented [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] smooth of relative dimension one over $T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $M,N$ be invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module] and let $a:M\to N$ be an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear morphism. Define its zero scheme $Z(a)\subseteq Y$ by the locally principal ideal $(b)$ wherever generators $m,n$ satisfy $a(m)=bn$ [def-pc-zero-scheme]. Fix an integer $d\geq0$. There is a unique open subscheme $T_d(a,U)\subseteq T$ such that, for every scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$, $h$ factors through $T_d(a,U)$ if and only if the pulled-back zero scheme $Z(a)\times_TT'$ is contained in $U_{T'}$, is a relative effective Cartier divisor on $Y_{T'}/T'$ [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier], and is finite locally free of rank $d$ over $T'$, meaning that it is finite and the pushforward of its structure sheaf is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{T'}^{\oplus d}$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Formation of this open commutes with arbitrary base change. Equivalently its field-valued points are exactly those where the fibre zero scheme is an effective Cartier divisor of length $d$ supported in the fibre of $U$. Empty zero schemes and $d=0$ are allowed. No reducedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 062Y (lemma-fibre-Cartier), especially (3), applied to the coefficient of a morphism of invertible modules. Properness removes the image of the closed complement of the relative Cartier neighbourhood and the image of Z(a) intersect (Y minus U). Finiteness and local freeness use more-morphisms.tex Tag 02LS (lemma-characterize-finite) and morphisms.tex Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat). This is an agent-formulated open-locus consequence, not the statement of any single tag.

proof.text: Put $Z=Z(a)$. Changing bases of $M,N$ multiplies the coefficient $b$ by a unit, so the ideals $(b)$ glue and $Z$ is locally principal. The morphism $a$ is the section of $N\otimes M^{-1}$ to which [def-pc-zero-scheme] applies. For any base change, the local identity $(B/(b))\otimes_A A'=(B\otimes_A A')/(b\otimes1)$ identifies its zero scheme with $Z\times_TT'$. This uses no flatness of $A'$. We will use this identity for all subsequent pullbacks. Let $G\subseteq |T|$ be the set of points $t$ where $Z_t$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $Y_t$ and is contained in $U_t$.

source.place: Local form of zero schemes; arbitrary scalar-extension quotient identity.

proof.text: Fix $t\in G$. For every $z\in Z_t$, apply [lem-pc-recd-fibre-cartier-local] to $p:Y\to T$, $Z$, and $z$. Flatness and local finite presentation are hypotheses of the item; local principality is Step 1. Obtain an open $V_z\subseteq Y$ on which $Z$ is relative effective Cartier. On $Y\setminus |Z|$ its ideal is the unit ideal, so the empty divisor is relative effective Cartier there. Let $W$ be the union of these opens. It contains the entire fibre $Y_t$, and $Z\cap W$ is relative effective Cartier because the generator and flatness conditions are local on the source [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. The closed sets $Y\setminus W$ and $|Z|\cap(Y\setminus U)$ have closed images under $p$, by the universally closed clause of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Neither image contains $t$. Their complementary intersection $V\subseteq T$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$, with $Y_V\subseteq W$ and $Z_V\subseteq U_V$. Thus $Z_V$ is relative effective Cartier on $Y_V/V$.

On $V$ of Step 2, restrict to the smooth relative curve $U_V/V$. The divisor $Z_V$ is closed in $U_V$ and relative effective Cartier there. The implication (2) to (3) of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion] gives local quasi-finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation of $Z_V\to V$, without a Noetherian assumption. Moreover $Y_V\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and its closed subscheme $Z_V$ is proper over $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] and then [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free]. Consequently $Z_V\to V$ is finite locally free. Its fibres are Cartier by [lem-pc-recd-pullback], applied to the flat finitely presented $Y_V/V$. Hence $V\subseteq G$. These neighbourhoods show that $G$ is open, and cover it by loci with the stated Cartier and finite locally free properties. Those properties agree on overlaps because the divisor is always the restriction of the same $Z$.

Write $q:Z_G\to G$. It is finite locally free by Step 3 (finiteness and the local free algebra description are local on the base). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant] to obtain the open and closed degree-$d$ piece $G_d$ of $G$. Set $T_d(a,U)=G_d$, with its open subscheme structure in $T$. On $G_d$ the algebra $q_*\mathcal O_{Z_G}$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O^{\oplus d}$: by [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free] it is $\mathcal O^{\oplus e}$ on an open neighbourhood of each $t\in G_d$, and by the algebra base-change isomorphism (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change] its fibre algebra $\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O)$ is $\kappa(t)^{\oplus e}$, so $e=d$. This is the rank-$d$ description used in Steps 5 and 7. Its residue fibres are exactly the Cartier zero schemes supported in $U$ with $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O)=d$. This is the length meant here; it includes the residue-field degrees of the closed points. In particular it is not merely the number of geometric support points.

Suppose $h:T'\to T$ factors through $G_d$. By [lem-pc-recd-pullback], the base change of $Z_{G_d}$ is relative effective Cartier on $Y_{T'}/T'$. Its support remains in $U_{T'}$. A finite morphism has affine inverse images [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. On affine opens of $G_d$ and $T'$, the pulled-back finite scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A')$; if $B\simeq A^{\oplus d}$ as a module, its new algebra is $(A')^{\oplus d}$. Such charts cover the base, so it is finite with locally free structure algebra of rank $d$. Equivalently, this is the algebra base-change isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change]. Thus all requested properties hold for every factoring $h$, including nonflat $h$.

Conversely suppose $Z'=Z\times_TT'$ has all the asserted properties. Fix $t'\in T'$, put $t=h(t')$, $k=\kappa(t)$ and $K=\kappa(t')$. Its fibre $Z'_ {t'}=Z_t\times_kK$ is Cartier: use [lem-pc-recd-pullback] for $Y_{T'}/T'$ and $Z'$. The required flatness and finite presentation of this ambient family follow on affine charts from tensor associativity (scalar extension of an exact tensor functor is exact) and extension of a finite list of algebra generators and relations. On every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $Y_t$ trivializing the two lines, multiplication by $b\otimes1$ on $C\otimes_kK$ is injective. The map $C\to C\otimes_kK$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat]. Injectivity reflection [lem-trf-faithfully-flat-ltensor-injective-reflection], applied to $C\xrightarrow{b}C$, gives injectivity before extension. Thus $Z_t$ is Cartier. Surjectivity of this spectrum map [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] also shows $Z_t\subseteq U_t$: any point in the complement would lift to a point of $Z'_ {t'}$ outside $U_{t'}$. Hence $t\in G$.

source.place: Tag 056Q; algebra.tex Tags 00HP, 00HQ, faithfully flat field-extension reflection.

proof.text: At the point $t$ of Step 6, Step 3 already makes $Z_t$ finite over $k$. The affine scalar-extension computation of Step 5 identifies its $K$-fibre algebra with $K\otimes_k\Gamma(Z_t,\mathcal O)$. By [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change], its dimension is unchanged. Since the given $Z'\to T'$ has rank $d$, this dimension is $d$, so $t\in G_d$. This holds for every $t'$, hence $h$ has image in $G_d$ and factors uniquely through the open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] (restrict the topological map and its structure-sheaf map). Combined with Step 5 this proves the universal property. Any other open with that property has exactly these residue-field points, so is the same open subscheme. For any $T_1\to T$, a test map $T'\to T_1$ factors through $G_d\times_TT_1$ exactly when its composite to $T$ does, exactly when the twice-pulled-back zero scheme has the required properties. Associativity of the fibre product identifies these with the properties of the pulled-back data. This proves arbitrary base-change compatibility and the field-valued formulation. For $d=0$ the algebra is locally the zero module, giving the empty scheme; all arguments also apply to an empty base or empty $U$.

The FIX adds the link: by lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free the pushforward is locally O^{⊕e}, and by lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change (2) its fibre algebra at t is κ(t)^{⊕e}, so e=d. Both nodes go into the step's uses; both were already in proof_deps, and only the proof field changes. Steps 1-7 hold. Step 1 identifies the base change by a quotient, so it needs no flatness, and it correctly avoids the flat-only lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties. Step 2 shrinks to a base neighbourhood using universal closedness on two closed sets. Step 3 gets finiteness from proper plus locally quasi-finite, and local freeness from finite, flat and lfp. Step 6 reflects the Cartier property to the field fibre by faithful flatness of C→C⊗_kK and by surjectivity on spectra. Step 7 gets dimension invariance from lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change, and uniqueness and base change follow. Small cases checked: empty base, a an isomorphism (giving T_0), a=0 on a smooth fibre (excluded), U empty, nonreduced base with nonflat h.
